## Abstract:

We describe an algorithm that, given an integral ideal $\mathfrak {A}$ in a number field $K$, finds the largest integer $k\geqslant 1$ such that $\mathfrak {A}$ is a $k$-th power, and at the same time computes the ideal $\mathfrak {B}$ such that $\mathfrak {A} = \mathfrak {B}^k$. This algorithm does not require the complete factorization of $\mathfrak {A}$ into a product of prime ideals; given the maximal order $\mathbb {Z}_K$, we prove that it has polynomial time complexity. We apply this algorithm to the reduction of elements of $K^*$ modulo $k$-th powers. References
